subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — FinLytics (SLOs & sizing)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finlytics.com>, Sarah Park <sarah@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery follow-up — Dedicated capacity SLOs & sizing

Hi Tom / Sarah,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate sizing for Dedicated capacity: 

Summary of SLOs discussed
- Latency targets: p95 <= 300 ms for short responses (<=128 tokens); p95 <= 800 ms for medium responses (129-512 tokens).
- Time-to-first-token (streaming) requirement: < 500 ms for p95. Partial streaming of tokens is required (client consumes tokens as they arrive).
- Throughput: steady-state target ~150 requests/sec with average request ~256 tokens; peak bursts up to 400 requests/sec for ~10-15 minutes.
- Concurrency: sustained concurrent requests of 16-24 during normal hours, peaks to 48.

Model profile / workload notes from your stack
- Typical completion lengths: avg 256 tokens, 95th ~1024 tokens.
- Many requests use streaming to render results progressively in the UI (chat + token-level highlights).
- Batchability: most requests are independent (low cross-request prefix overlap) — so batching helps but cache hit rate will be low.

Initial sizing guidance (ballpark)
- H100 (80GB) cluster: recommended starting config = 4 x H100 GPUs reserved. Expected to meet latency SLOs for short and medium responses and sustain throughput with efficient batching. H100 gives ~1.5-1.8x throughput advantage vs A100 for fp16 workloads and handles long sequences better.
- A100 (40GB) cluster: recommended starting config = 8 x A100 GPUs reserved (or mixed sizing). A100 can be cost-effective for shorter sequences but will need more GPUs to match H100 peak throughput.
- Other notes: If you use int8/4-bit quantized models we can provide slightly higher density on A100 but will need validation for quality impact.

Benchmarking we recommend before commit
1) 2-hour sustained run at expected average load (150 rps) to validate steady-state latency and memory pressure.
2) Burst test (400 rps) for 15 minutes to validate autoscale/burst capacity and tail latency.
3) Streaming validation focusing on time-to-first-token and token-per-second delivery.

I attached a quick sizing workbook (dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx) and our public performance benchmarks (redwood-performance-benchmarks.pdf) to help you map loads to GPU counts.

Proposed next steps
- Confirm a 2-hour pilot window next week (we can host a reserved small cluster for testing).
- Share a representative request trace or sample payloads (we can replay them).
- Marissa will coordinate scheduling and the test matrix.

If this matches your expectations I can schedule the pilot and loop in infra for a bench run.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finlytics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Park <sarah@finlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up — Dedicated capacity SLOs & sizing

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Streaming: yes, partial token streaming is required. We rely on first-token latency to keep the UI snappy. Is streaming handled at the request-level (i.e., you stream partial outputs as tokens are generated) or do you require chunking at the app layer?

2) Request characteristics: our current 90-day telemetry shows avg 240-270 tokens, median ~180, 95th around 1024, as you called out. Peak concurrency yesterday hit ~52 for about 8 minutes.

3) Quality: we plan to run the production model in fp16. If you recommend quantized int8 for density, we will want a small sample A/B to validate output fidelity. 

4) Can you confirm what the 2-hour pilot would look like practically — will it be a reserved cluster under our account, or hosted by Redwood (you quoted reserved capacity earlier)? Also what's the expected setup time and whether we need to open ports or provide IP allowlists?

We'll share sample payloads (anonymized) by EOD. Can you also include estimated monthly committed cost ranges for the H100 vs A100 starting configs you suggested?

Thanks — Tom
Tom Lee

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finlytics.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Discovery follow-up — Dedicated capacity performance validation

Thanks Tom — great questions, I'll coordinate the pilot. Operational details and proposed test plan below.

Pilot logistics (proposed)
- Provisioning: Redwood will provision a temporary dedicated cluster in your cloud account (AWS account link) for the 2-hour validation. This lets you validate actual networking and IAM without moving data out of your environment. We can also run the test in Redwood-hosted infra if you prefer — both are supported.
- Networking: we'll need a short list of IPs for IP allowlist or a VPC peering step — I'll send the network checklist after you confirm the pilot.
- Test matrix (attached workbook):
  * Test A: Steady-state 2 hours at 150 rps (avg 256 tokens) — collect p50/p95/p99 latency, time-to-first-token, CPU/GPU utilization, and token/sec.
  * Test B: Burst 15 minutes at 400 rps — verify tail latency and any queuing/backpressure behavior.
  * Test C: Streaming verification — 1 hour of simulated streaming sessions to measure time-to-first-token and throughput per stream.
  * Test D: Quality check — small A/B between fp16 and int8 on a subset of requests (we will not change model weights; we'll use quantized execution where available).
- Deliverables from Redwood: raw traces, aggregated latency & throughput charts, recommended reserved GPU counts (H100 vs A100), and a short readout call to review results.

Cost estimate (very rough)
- 4 x H100 reserved cluster = projected committed monthly cost range: $XXk–$YYk (final quote after we nail down region and utilization).
- 8 x A100 reserved cluster = projected committed monthly cost range: $WWk–$ZZk.

Next steps
1) Tom — confirm preferred pilot window next week (we have Tue/Wed mornings available).
2) Share anonymized sample payloads (thank you).
3) I'll send the network checklist and a calendar invite once we lock a slot.

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-sheet.xlsx, redwood-performance-benchmarks.pdf

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
